title: Rigveda 8.29: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.29: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.29 is a hymn of 10 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 603r-603v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.29.1-2 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 2, varga 36); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 603r
translation.original_text:
1ba̱bhrur eko̱ viṣu̍ṇaḥ sū̱naro̱ yuvā̱ñjy a̍ṅkte hira̱ṇyaya̍m ||
2yoni̱m eka̱ ā sa̍sāda̱ dyota̍no̱ 'ntar de̱veṣu̱ medhi̍raḥ ||
translation.text:
1ONE is a youth brown, active, manifold he decks the golden one with ornament.
2Another, luminous, occupies the place of sacrifice, Sage, among the Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 603r (numbered 25r by the scribe) (OPenn image 603, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.27.21 ‹ut-ite yat madhyandine ātuci›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 603v (numbered 25v by the scribe), begins in RV 8.29.3 ‹-antaḥ deveṣu ni-dhruviḥ›. Verses 8.29.1-2 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1babhruḥ | ekaḥ | viṣuṇaḥ | sūnaraḥ | yuvā | añji | aṅkte | hiraṇyayam
2yonim | ekaḥ | ā | sasāda | dyotanaḥ | antaḥ | deveṣu | medhiraḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 8.29.3-10 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 2, varga 36); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 603v
translation.original_text:
3vāśī̱m eko̍ bibharti̱ hasta̍ āya̱sīm a̱ntar de̱veṣu̱ nidhru̍viḥ ||
4vajra̱m eko̍ bibharti̱ hasta̱ āhi̍ta̱ṁ tena̍ vṛ̱trāṇi̍ jighnate ||
5ti̱gmam eko̍ bibharti̱ hasta̱ āyu̍dha̱ṁ śuci̍r u̱gro jalā̍ṣabheṣajaḥ ||
6pa̱tha eka̍ḥ pīpāya̱ taska̍ro yathām̐ e̱ṣa ve̍da nidhī̱nām ||
7trīṇy eka̍ urugā̱yo vi ca̍krame̱ yatra̍ de̱vāso̱ mada̍nti ||
8vibhi̱r dvā ca̍rata̱ eka̍yā sa̱ha pra pra̍vā̱seva̍ vasataḥ ||
9sado̱ dvā ca̍krāte upa̱mā di̱vi sa̱mrājā̍ sa̱rpirā̍sutī ||
10arca̍nta̱ eke̱ mahi̱ sāma̍ manvata̱ tena̱ sūrya̍m arocayan ||
translation.text:
3One brandishes in his hand an iron knife, firm, in his seat amid the Deities.
4Another holds the thunderbolt, wherewith he slays the Vr̥itras, resting in his hand.
5Another bears a pointed weapon: bright is he, and strong, with healing medicines.
6Another, thief-like, watches well the ways, and knows the places where the treasures lie.
7Another with his mighty stride hath made his three steps thither where the Gods rejoice.
8Two with one Dame ride on with winged steeds, and journey forth like travellers on their way.
9Two, highest, in the heavens have set their seat, worshipped with holy oil, imperial Kings.
10Some, singing lauds, conceived the Sâma-hymn, great hymn whereby they caused the Sun to shine.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 603v (numbered 25v by the scribe) (OPenn image 604, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.29.3 ‹-antaḥ deveṣu ni-dhruviḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 604r (numbered 26r by the scribe), begins in RV 8.30.4 ‹-asmabhyam śarma sa-prathaḥ gave›. Verses 8.29.3-10 end on this page; 8.29.3 begins on fol. 603r (numbered 25r by the scribe).

5tigmam | ekaḥ | bibharti | haste | āyudham | śuciḥ | ugraḥ | jalāṣa-bheṣajaḥ
6pathaḥ | ekaḥ | pīpāya | taskaraḥ | yathā | eṣaḥ | veda | ni-dhīnām
